newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain rules out using privatisation to cut deficit.
newsitem.headline: Spain rules out using privatisation to cut deficit.

text.p: Spain's Budget Secretary Jose Folgado ruled out on Wednesday using privatisation receipts to cut the budget deficit.

"Income is adjusting perfectly to forecasts and all the analysis that we're doing to reach the public deficit target exludes income from privatisations. The income from privatisations will go basically to reducing public debt and never directly to reducing the public deficit," Folgado told journalists.
The government has not as yet, however, specified what it will do with taxes on capital gains from, for example, the sale of its final stake in domestic telephone giant Telefonica.

The Exchequer will receive a total of 180 billion pesetas via two corporate tax payments from state holding SEPPa --under which the Telefonica stake was administered-- as capital gains on the privatisation, Economy Vice-secretary Fernando Diaz Moreno said in February.
